import Base

# A Moore sum is a rolling three-column box sum with its focus removed.
def Life.stencil(
  +here: List<&2, U32>,
  +north: List<&2, U32>,
  +south: List<&2, U32>,
  west: U32
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match here:
    case Nil{}:
      Nil{}
    case cell <> eastward:
      n = Maybe.default(&2, U32, List.head(&2, U32, north), 0)
      ne = Maybe.default(
        &2, U32, List.head(&2, U32, List.tail(&2, U32, north)), 0)
      e = Maybe.default(&2, U32, List.head(&2, U32, eastward), 0)
      s = Maybe.default(&2, U32, List.head(&2, U32, south), 0)
      se = Maybe.default(
        &2, U32, List.head(&2, U32, List.tail(&2, U32, south)), 0)
      +middle = (n + cell + s : U32)
      east = (ne + e + se : U32)
      +neighbors = (west + middle + east - cell : U32)
      # Two keeps; three creates.
      Bool.pick(
        U32,
        U32.is_eq(neighbors, 2),
        cell,
        Bool.to_u32(U32.is_eq(neighbors, 3))) <>
        Life.stencil(
          eastward,
          List.tail(&2, U32, north),
          List.tail(&2, U32, south),
          middle)

# The consumed row becomes north; the remaining board exposes south.
def Life.sweep(
  height: Nat,
  +width: Nat,
  +cells: List<&2, U32>,
  north: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match height:
    case 0n:
      Nil{}
    case 1n+more:
      +here = List.take(&2, U32, cells, width)
      +below = List.drop(&2, U32, cells, width)
      south = List.take(&2, U32, below, width)
      List.append(
        &2,
        U32,
        Life.stencil(here, north, south, 0),
        Life.sweep(more, width, below, here))

def step(
  width: U32, height: U32, cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  Life.sweep(
    U32.to_nat(height),
    U32.to_nat(width),
    cells,
    Nil{})

def evolve(
  turns: Nat, +width: U32, +height: U32, cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match turns:
    case 0n:
      cells
    case 1n+more:
      evolve(more, width, height, step(width, height, cells))
hypothesis: The repeated grids, mirrored triples, and disappearing centers suggest a rolling three-column interpretation: each Moore neighborhood is the sum of west, middle, and east columns with the focused cell removed. The concrete improvement hypothesis is that streaming those row windows directly—and expressing B3/S23 as “two keeps; three creates”—will make the boundary behavior and rule composition more immediate than materializing an intermediate matrix.
findings: No semantic findings: the prior implementation passed all behavioral, composition, backend, and semantic checks. The style finding is confirmed. This revision removes the separate Life.rows pass, the allocated dead row, and the final concatenation layer. Life.sweep now streams the flat board, empty lists supply dead boundaries, and Life.stencil carries one column sum instead of three individual west cells.
